answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed bond in scarce currency for a 30-day horizon before bidding on jobs, such as inspecting a lantern on a knoll. Creating extra names does not create extra bidding capacity for free: each must post its own bond, and one bond cannot back two active identities. An attacker running a thousand sybils must therefore immobilize a thousand bonds, paying the capital cost throughout the lockup.
